name: Audit Trail TSA timestamping
description: Anchors chain heads to a qualified RFC-3161 Time-Stamping Authority; each round-trip lands as a chained tsa_timestamp row carrying the TSR, verified offline with openssl.
project_description: Submodule of audit_trail. Anchors a chain head's hash to a qualified RFC-3161 Time-Stamping Authority: build a TimeStampReq (via openssl ts -query) with the head hash as message imprint, POST it to the configured TSA over the Guzzle http_client, capture the TimeStampResp, synchronously verify it (openssl ts -verify with the pinned CA cert + nonce echo) and record a chained tsa_timestamp row carrying the base64 TSR/TSQ and their SHA-256s in the permanent bucket. Because the TSR is signed by a third-party key, forging the chain later would also require forging every historical timestamp. TSAs are audit_trail_tsa_provider config entities (URL, pinned CA cert, nonce toggle, and auth: none/basic/bearer/mtls with all secrets resolved at request time from drupal/key entities and mTLS material written to short-lived 0600 temp files). Runs from cron (per-chain throttle) or on demand (drush audit_trail:timestamp, audit_trail:verify-timestamp, UI actions). Requires the openssl binary on the host (reported on the status page).
